title: Contract catalogue and code generation
claim_boundary: Source-verified implementation only; higher evidence levels require the named open gates. Path presence is not behavioural proof; assertion-level traceability governs implementation claims.

assertions.statement: Validate all JSON Schemas and examples
open_gates: Generate and compare Rust-derived schemas after compiler bootstrap.
assertions.permitted_claim: All checked-in JSON Schemas and examples are statically validated; Rust-generation parity is not yet proven.

assertions.statement: Generate schemas from Rust types and diff against checked-in canonical forms
open_gates: Install Rust and generate schemas from Rust types.
Diff generated output against canonical schemas.
assertions.permitted_claim: Rust types and canonical schemas coexist, but code-generation parity is not claimed.

assertions.statement: Add compatibility fixtures and migration/version rules
open_gates: Add semantic compatibility fixtures and migration tests before a stable release.
assertions.permitted_claim: Exact schema, WIT, OpenAPI and MCP surface drift is gated; semantic compatibility remains separate.

assertions.statement: Add report/study linkage and protocol-amendment contracts
open_gates: Compile and exercise report/study and amendment invariants.
assertions.permitted_claim: Report/study linkage and protocol-amendment contracts are checked in and statically validated.

assertions.statement: Generate TypeScript/Python bindings only as thin contract packages
open_gates: Generate thin TypeScript and Python contract packages only after the neutral schema surface stabilises.
assertions.permitted_claim: Bindings are planned but not implemented.

open_gates: Add compiler and downstream-consumer columns to release evidence.
assertions.permitted_claim: The schema catalogue and assertion traceability form a static conformance matrix; runtime conformance is not claimed.
